1.stem_plain: The students were reminded to abide _________ the school rules as outlined in the Student Handbook.

2.stem_plain: Not a single passenger _________ hurt when the bus skidded on the wet road.

3.stem_plain: Bernadette looked _________ than happy when she was not selected for the basketball trials that she had trained hard for.

4.stem_plain: _________ you decide not to go on the school trip, you will get a refund.

6.stem_plain: Peter continued with the marathon _________ being tired.

7.stem_plain: Shanice _________ on the grass and gazed at the stars in awe.

8.stem_plain: By the end of next month, Mr Tan _________ a trained instructor.

9.stem_plain: "I practised hard for the competition, but so _________ all the other competitors," Dan said.

10.stem_plain: Kelly suddenly spotted a suspicious person _________ in the school canteen.

1.zh: 学生须遵守学生手册中的校规。
1.note: 固定搭配 abide by；应选（3）by。

2.concept: 主谓一致 — Not a single + 单数
2.zh: 巴士在湿路上打滑时，没有一名乘客受伤。
2.note: not a single 后接单数谓语 was；应选（3）。

3.zh: 贝纳黛特未入选篮球选拔，看起来并不高兴。
3.note: 习语 less than happy；应选（2）less。

4.zh: 若决定不参加学校旅行，可获退款。

5.note: 附加问与 has 一致；应选（2）has。

6.zh: 彼得尽管疲惫仍继续跑马拉松。
6.note: despite + being tired 表让步；应选（2）despite。

7.zh: 香妮躺在草地上仰望星空。

8.zh: 到下月底，陈先生将成为持证教练。
8.note: 句首的By the end of next month（到下个月底为止）是一个非常典型的将来完成时标志词。当句子包含 by + 将来时间 时，通常表示在未来某一个时间点之前，某项动作将会被完成。

9.zh: 丹说：“我刻苦训练，其他选手也一样。”
9.note: so 倒装与过去式 practised 一致，用 did；应选（2）did。

10.zh: 凯莉发现有人在食堂游荡。

11.stem_plain: The teacher's _________ remarks brought a blush to Konan's cheeks and a smile to his face.

12.stem_plain: A series of tornadoes left a _________ of destruction across the country.

13.stem_plain: Even though Fiona is an award-winning writer in Southeast Asia, she remains _________ outside the region.

14.stem_plain: Having been in the same job for many years, Mrs Lee decided to _________ on her own and start a business.

15.stem_plain: Mrs Lim encouraged her daughter to read _________ by sharing with her a wide variety of books.

11.zh: 老师奉承的话让柯南脸红又微笑。
11.note: 应选（3）flattering；其余三项语气不合。

choices.zh: 贬低的，轻视的；小看的（形容词/动词现在分词，指用言语或态度将某人、某事物的价值、成就或重要性贬得很低，使其显得微不足道或毫无价值）
choices.eg: The team manager reminded everyone that making belittling remarks about a colleague's mistakes would only damage workplace morale and teamwork.

choices.zh: 傲慢的，高傲的；目中无人的（形容词，指一个人自视甚高，因自满而对他人表现出极其不屑、冷漠、甚至看不起的傲慢态度）
choices.eg: The wealthy businessman's haughty demeanor made it extremely difficult for the local community leaders to discuss the charity project with him.

choices.zh: 奉承的，讨好的；使人显得更漂亮的（形容词，指说赞美、恭维的话来取悦他人，或者形容衣着、光线或言论能很好地衬托出某人的优点）
choices.eg: The class teacher's genuinely flattering remarks about his outstanding art project brought a warm blush to Konan's cheeks and a proud smile to his face.

choices.zh: 伤感的，多愁善感的；带有情感色彩的（形容词，指极易受到情绪、过去的回忆或温情所影响，往往表现出过度的怀旧、悲伤或温柔的情感）
choices.eg: She kept all her old secondary school textbooks and uniform out of purely sentimental value, even though they were no longer of any practical use.

12.zh: 龙卷风在全国留下破坏痕迹。

choices.zh: 痕迹，足迹；（破坏的）后遗痕迹（名词，指人、动物或风暴移动时在地面上留下的长条状痕迹，常用于形容灾难过后留下的满目疮痍）
choices.eg: A series of violent tornadoes swept through the region, leaving a devastating trail of destruction and flattened houses across the country.

choices.zh: 路线，路途；固定航线（名词，指从一个地方到另一个地方所经过的预定道路、特定方向，或者公共交通工具的固定行驶路线）
choices.eg: The delivery drivers were instructed to map out the most efficient route using GPS to avoid the heavy rush-hour traffic in the city centre.

choices.zh: 环路，巡回路线；电路（名词，指一条起点和终点相同、呈环状的闭合路线，亦可指法官、运动员的巡回线路或电子学中的电流回路）
choices.eg: The professional racing drivers managed to complete fifteen laps around the challenging street circuit before the heavy downpour forced a suspension.

choices.zh: 通道，走廊；（文章的）段落（名词，指建筑物内、地下或船上连接不同区域的狭长通道，亦指书本、乐曲中被摘录出的一段内容）
choices.eg: The ancient castle featured a narrow secret passage hidden behind a heavy bookshelf that led straight down to the underground cellar.

13.zh: 菲奥娜在东南亚获奖，区外仍默默无闻。

choices.zh: 不知名的，不为人知的（指不被大众所了解、熟悉或认知的，名气不大的状态）
choices.eg: Even though Fiona is an award-winning writer in Southeast Asia, she remains unknown outside the region.

choices.zh: 难以忍受的，不可忍受的（指痛苦、压力、酷热等极其严重，超出了人所能承受的生理或心理极限）
choices.eg: The afternoon heat in the unconditioned classroom became unbearable, making it difficult for the students to focus.

choices.zh: 无法战胜的，无敌的；（价格）极具竞争力的（指在比赛、商业竞争中表现完美以至无人能击败）
choices.eg: With thirty consecutive match victories, the school's basketball team has proven themselves to be unbeatable this season.

choices.zh: 难忘的，终生难忘的（指某次经历、美景或事件因为极其美好、独特或深刻而永远留在记忆中）
choices.eg: The primary school graduation night was an unforgettable experience filled with emotional speeches and laughter.

choices.zh: 结交（朋友），开始（交谈）；（乐队）开始演奏（指主动与人攀谈、建立交情，或音乐突然响起）
choices.eg: The friendly traveler managed to strike up a cheerful conversation with the person sitting next to him on the train.

choices.zh: 从名单中划掉，吊销（执照）（指官方机构将某人的名字正式除名，或取消其专业执业资格）
choices.eg: The medical council decided to strike off the dishonest doctor from the official register for violating safety rules.

choices.zh: 自立门户，独立闯荡；开创（新路）（指离开原有的舒适圈或依赖的人，靠自己去发展新事业或新生活）
choices.eg: Having been in the same job for many years, Mrs Lee decided to strike out on her own and start a baking business.

choices.zh: 推翻（法律），判决无效；击倒，使病倒（指最高法院废除法律，或疾病、不幸突然降临击垮某人）
choices.eg: The high court voted to strike down the outdated regulation because it violated the fundamental rights of citizens.

15.zh: 林太太鼓励女儿广泛阅读。

choices.zh: 迅速地，准时地（指毫无延迟地立即行动，或在约定的精确时间做某事）
choices.eg: The medical team responded promptly to the emergency call, arriving at the scene within ten minutes.

choices.zh: 用功地，刻苦地；故意地（指花很多时间极其认真地学习或工作，也可指刻意避开某事）
choices.eg: The young student sat at his desk and studiously revised his science notes throughout the entire weekend.

choices.zh: 慷慨地，大方地（指乐于给予金钱、时间、赞美或帮助，数量往往超出一般预期）
choices.eg: The wealthy businessman contributed generously to the building fund, enabling the orphanage to expand its kitchen.

choices.zh: 广泛地，大规模地（指涉及很大的范围、深度、数量或广度，常与读书、研究、改建连用）
choices.eg: Mrs Lim encouraged her daughter to read extensively by sharing with her a wide variety of fiction and non-fiction books.

16.concept: 近义词 — inaugurated（开幕/投入使用）
16.note: 动词 inaugurated 意为正式开幕、投入使用。在描述大型项目、公园或设施对公众首次开放的完形考点语境中，及物动词 launched 意为推出、公开发行，是其最精准的近义词替换。
16.zh: 两个月后闪亮乐园将开幕。

choices.zh: 发起，开始，创始
choices.eg: The department supervisor initiated a research project to upgrade the website security system.

choices.zh: 触发，引起，引发（突发事件）
choices.eg: The thick smoke from the basement immediately triggered the automated fire alarm system.

choices.zh: 推出，正式开放，公开发行，发射
choices.eg: The grand theme park was officially launched last night, attracting thousands of eager visitors.

choices.zh: 起源于，来自，开创（常与 from 连用）
choices.eg: The prominent scientist originally originated the creative layout design during his field study.

17.concept: 近义词 — revolutionary（革命性的/新颖的）
17.note: 形容词 revolutionary 意为革命性的、前所未有的、彻底突破传统的。在修饰某种全新的、市面上罕见的前沿体验时，形容词 novel 意为新颖的、新奇的，属于直接对标的近义代换。
17.zh: 游客将体验这座新颖主题乐园。

choices.zh: 新颖的，新奇的，异常的（作形容词）；长篇小说（作名词）
choices.eg: Traveling inside the space-themed capsule provided a truly novel experience for the primary school pupils.

choices.zh: 异国风情的，奇特的，外来的
choices.eg: The newly opened holiday resort serves a wide selection of exotic food from South America.

choices.zh: 未来主义的，超前的，前卫的
choices.eg: The newly designed exhibition hall features a futuristic architectural layout with shiny metal beams.

choices.zh: 传统的，常规的，因循守旧的
choices.eg: Local organic farmers decided to avoid conventional chemical fertilizers to protect the local environment.

18.concept: 近义词 — unparalleled（无与伦比的）
18.note: 形容词 unparalleled 意为无与伦比的、无可比拟的。在商业宣传或景区描写其体验没有对手、顶尖卓越时，对应的核心学术形容词近义词为 unrivalled（无双的，无敌的，没有对手的）。
18.zh: 乐园承诺无与伦比的体验。

choices.zh: 不寻常的，独特的，罕见的
choices.eg: It was an unusual sight to see heavy snow falling along the tropical sandy beach.

choices.zh: 无双的，无敌的，无可比拟的
choices.eg: Guests staying at the luxury hotel can enjoy an unrivalled view of the entire city skyline.

choices.zh: 少见的，罕见的，不凡的
choices.eg: The young classical pianist showed uncommon talent during the national competition yesterday.

choices.zh: 被低估的（作过去分词/形容词）
choices.eg: The coach admitted that they completed the marathon with an underestimated amount of effort.

19.note: 短语 draws near 意为（时间、日子等）临近、逼近。在描写某个特定节点、日期逐渐靠近的命题语境下，不及物动词 approaches 意为接近、临近，是其直接对标的学术近义词。
19.zh: 开幕日日益临近，期待升温。

choices.zh: （危险/困难等）阴森地逼近，隐现
choices.eg: A sense of deep danger looms as the travelers stepped closer toward the dark forest area.

choices.zh: 前进，推进，（时间）流逝
choices.eg: As modern technology rapidly advances, human life expectancy has climbed significantly.

choices.zh: 汇聚，相交（指线条、路径、意见等集中于一点）
choices.eg: The two narrow mountain trails smoothly converge near the entrance gate of the old castle.

choices.zh: 临近，靠近，接近
choices.eg: As the grand opening day steadily approaches, public anticipation across the city continues to rise.

20.note: 名词 festivities 意为庆祝活动、庆典、欢庆。在描写公众、游客或市民集体参与热闹活动的学术完形语境下，名词 celebrations（庆祝活动，庆典）是其完美的等义词代换。
20.zh: 开幕日众人将参与庆典。

choices.zh: 正规手续，礼节，例行公事
choices.eg: The international businessman spent two hours completing the legal formalities at the airport counter.

choices.zh: 促销活动，晋升，推广宣传
choices.eg: The shopping center organized extensive store promotions to attract more buyers during holidays.

choices.zh: 庆祝活动，庆典，赞美
choices.eg: Thousands of excited residents gathered near the town square to join the annual grand celebrations.

choices.zh: （宗教/节日）仪式的举行，遵守，奉行
choices.eg: The local community is highly strict about maintaining their traditional religious observances.

cloze: Can't wait to immerse yourself in a day of fun within a virtual world? When Sparklyland is [Q16 (inaugurated)] in two months' time, you can! Armed with headsets and virtual goggles, visitors to this [Q17 (revolutionary)] theme park will experience a virtual world of rides and games.

The theme park's upcoming opening has generated much fanfare. Promising its visitors an experience that is [Q18 (unparalleled)], public anticipation has intensified as the official opening day [Q19 (draws near)]. A huge crowd is expected to join in the [Q20 (festivities)] on its opening day. The success of this theme park will mark the start of a new era of entertainment.
zh: 迫不及待想沉浸于虚拟世界？两个月后闪亮乐园开幕，戴上头盔与护目镜即可体验虚拟游乐项目。
开幕引发热议；乐园承诺无与伦比体验，开幕日临近，众人将共庆，标志娱乐新时代。

21.stem_plain: Which of the following is true of "Green Park Grand Opening" event?

options.1: All participants must learn about gardening in the park.
options.2: The activities will be carried out every month for the public.
options.3: Visitors can enjoy the concert that is conducted in the morning.
options.4: Guided walks of the nature reserve are carried out on an hourly basis.

22.stem_plain: Jenny plans to visit the park. If she takes Bus 28, which is the most direct route to Green Park?

options.1: Alight at Hyber Road and enter via the Side Gate.
options.2: Alight at Hyber Road and enter via the Main Gate.
options.3: Alight at Compass Road and enter via the Side Gate.
options.4: Alight at Compass Road and enter via the Main Gate.

23.stem_plain: What is allowed throughout Green Park?

24.stem_plain: Which of the following can be said about the activity, **'Ramblings of Nature'**?

options.1: Every visitor will receive a free booklet of poems.
options.2: The poet was inspired by nature conservationists.
options.3: Visitors will need to download a mobile app for a small fee.
options.4: Visitors can listen to poems being recited by the poet in person.

25.stem_plain: Mr Tan is at Green Horizon Nature Reserve and facing the lake. Which of the following is true?

options.1: He can walk towards the lake to get to the photo exhibition.
options.2: The toilet nearest to him is at the Visitor Centre near the main gate.
options.3: The "Music Oasis" Concert in the Park is some distance away to his right.
options.4: He will find the Gift Shop nearer to him than the Children's Adventure Grove.

26.stem_plain: Based on the newsletter article, avid photographers can expect _________.

options.2: a guided journey on Singapore's success
options.3: guaranteed prizes upon submission of photographs
options.4: photographs of nature taken from different viewpoints

27.stem_plain: A gentle reminder was included in the article. The writers added that to remind visitors _________.

options.1: to walk barefooted in the park
options.2: to leave their footprints in the park
options.3: not to take photographs in the park
options.4: not to remove anything from the park

28.stem_plain: What is the main purpose of the flyer?

options.1: to inform readers of the event highlights
options.2: to encourage readers to pay a visit to the park
options.3: to showcase Green Park's location and land mass
options.4: to promote the works of local artists and arts groups

23.note: Dos: pets leashed allowed; drones restricted; no yelling; stay on trails.

24.note: Ramblings of Nature: poet inspired by conservationists; free app.

25.note: At lake facing reserve: concert to his right, some distance away.

26.note: Photo contest: nature from different viewpoints, dawn to dusk.

27.note: Gentle reminder: not remove anything from park.

28.note: Main purpose: encourage a visit to Green Park.

cloze: Have you ever wondered what the Earth looked like 300 million years ago? [Q29] were swamps and marshes everywhere and it was warmer than it [Q30] today. Ancient trees, ferns and plants grew everywhere. Very weird-looking animals roamed the Earth, and fish that looked [Q31] stranger lived deep in the oceans and seas.

When [Q32] prehistoric plants and animals died, their bodies decomposed in the same way [Q33] organisms do today. The dead organisms became buried [Q34] layers of mud, rock, sand and water. Gradually, these layers built up and [Q35] began to exert a great amount of pressure [Q36] the layers below it.

As millions of years passed, the decomposed plants and animals formed different types of fossil fuels such as coal, oil and natural gas. The type of fossil fuels that formed depended on whether it was the remains [Q37] plants or animals or both, and [Q38] long the organisms had been buried. It also depended on the temperature and pressure conditions during the decay of the organisms.
zh: 你可曾想过三亿年前地球是什么模样？那时遍地沼泽湿地，气候比今天更暖。古老的树木、蕨类与植物四处生长；模样古怪的动物在陆地漫游，深海与近海中则栖息着长得更加怪异的鱼类。
当这些史前动植物死亡后，它们的遗体以与今天生物相同的方式分解，并被掩埋在层层泥浆、岩石、沙土与水体之下。渐渐地，这些地层不断增厚，每一层都对下方的地层施加巨大压力。
历经数百万年，腐烂的动植物形成了煤、石油、天然气等不同化石燃料。形成的种类取决于遗骸来自植物、动物或两者兼有，以及生物被埋藏了多久，也取决于分解过程中的温度与压力条件。

29.note: There were swamps and marshes everywhere 存在句用 there。 故填'M — there'。

30.note: warmer than it is today 与现在比较，用 is。 故填'G — is'。

31.note: looked even stranger 比较级前加强语气 even。 故填'D — even'。

32.note: 指前文 prehistoric plants and animals → these。 故填'N — these'。

33.note: the same way as organisms do today → as。 故填'A — as'。

34.note: buried under layers 埋在……之下。 故填'P — under'。

35.note: each of the layers 各层分别施压（键注 part of the layers）。 故填'C — each'。

36.note: pressure on the layers below。 故填'L — on'。

37.note: remains of plants or animals。 故填'K — of'。

38.note: how long the organisms had been buried。 故填'F — how'。

cloze: Have you ever played multiplayer video games or even just watched someone else play? If you had, you would know how [Q39(triling)] these games can be. In many ways, competitive video games are very similar [Q40(with)] traditional sports such as basketball or soccer. Players train, practise, and develop their [Q41(profeesiency)] in their chosen game in an effort to [Q42(being)] the best. They develop new strategies and [Q43(teknicks)] . However, instead of working on how to run faster or throw a ball [Q44(most)] correctly, video game players focus more on [Q45(trained)] their minds, reflexes, and finger dexterity to [Q46(xccell)] on a virtual playing field. Finally, they face off against each other in [Q47(inttennce)] head-to-head matches.

Today, more and more people are taking video games [Q48(seriousness)] as a new kind of competitive sport. [Q49(Know)] as e-sports, these professional video game competitions are drawing [Q50(masieve)] audiences. These competitions are also turning the best players into worldwide celebrities.
zh: 多人游戏很刺激；竞技游戏与传统运动相似，选手苦练技巧。
人们日益认真看待电竞；顶尖选手成为全球明星。

cloze: A map is a drawing of all or part of the Earth's surface. Its basic [Q51] is to show where things are. Maps may show visible features, such as lakes, buildings and roads. They may also show things that cannot be [Q52], such as boundaries and temperatures. Many maps show the location and shape of features on the Earth's surface. These often [Q53] of natural and man-made features within the area represented. [Q54] maps show the boundaries of countries and cities, or even the climate of different areas.

Maps are typically drawn on a flat surface. A map displayed on a spherical surface is called a globe. While globes can provide the [Q55] information as flat maps, it is a more [Q56] representation. This is because a spherical globe shows the Earth as it [Q57] like when observed from outer space.

Unlike modern maps, [Q58] maps had drawings to show locations of features like castles and mountains. To [Q59] that the drawings were clear, they were painted on large canvases. Such maps were nice to look at and easy to understand. [Q60], as more details were included, they became cluttered. [Q61] time, maps were made simpler. Modern mapmakers [Q62] drawings with symbols. Each symbol represents one particular thing. Features such as cities, rivers and railroads are represented [Q63] different symbols. For [Q64], double black lines with red between them can be a symbol for a main road. [Q65] to maps with drawings, such maps contain more details and are still easy to read. Given the variety of symbols, a legend is therefore included to describe their usage in maps.
zh: 地图是地球表面全部或部分的绘图。它的基本功能是显示事物的位置。地图可以显示可见特征，如湖泊、建筑和道路；也可以显示不可见的特征，如边界和气温。许多地图显示地表特征的位置和形状，这些通常由所代表区域内的自然和人造特征组成。有些地图则显示国家和城市的边界，甚至是不同地区的气候。
地图通常画在平面上。显示在球体表面上的地图被称为地球仪。虽然地球仪可以提供与平面地图相同的信息，但它是一种更准确的呈现方式。这是因为球形地球仪展示了地球从外太空观察时的真实样貌。

与现代地图不同，早期的地图用图画来显示城堡和山脉等特征的位置。为了确保图画清晰，它们被画在巨大的画布上。这类地图既美观又易懂。然而，随着包含的细节越来越多，它们变得杂乱无章。随着时间的推移，地图变得更加简洁。现代地图制作者用符号取代了图画。每个符号代表一个特定的事物。城市、河流和铁路等特征由不同的符号表示。例如，中间带红色的双黑线可以作为主干道的符号。与带有图画的地图相比，此类地图包含更多细节，且依然易于阅读。鉴于符号的多样性，地图中通常会附上图例来描述它们的用法。

51.note: 用来形容地图的核心存在目的与作用。指地图的基本“功能”、“目的”、“角色”或“任务”就是展示事物所处的位置，故填入名词 function / purpose / role / objective / goal / job。

52.concept: 被动语态动词原形搭配
52.note: 前面有助动词情态结构 cannot be，后接过去分词构成被动语态。与前文提到的“可见特征（visible features）”形成鲜明正反意照，指边界、气温等无法被肉眼直接“看见”、“观察到”或“感知”的抽象事物，故填 seen / observed / noticed / perceived。

53.note: 主语为复数代词 These（指代前文的多种地表特征），陈述客观事实用一般现在时，且后文紧跟介词 of。完美契合高频常考的经典专属搭配 consist of，意为这些特征“由”自然和人造景观“所构成/组成”。

54.note: 修饰复数名词 maps。前文已经论述了“许多地图（Many maps）”，此处与之形成平行的分组对比，引入“其他的（Other）”或者是“一些（Some）”能够展现国家边界或气候特征的地图。位于句首需大写。

55.note: 与其前置的定冠词 the 和后置的名词 information 完美结合。构成全行业、各类书面语体中极高频考核的经典专属平行习语 the same information... as...，意为球状地球仪能够提供与平面地图“完全相同的”信息。

56.concept: 形容词语意修饰与科学对比
56.note: 前面有比较级限制词 more，修饰名词 representation（再现/表征）。由于地球仪是三维球体，能避免平面投影的扭曲，因此它是一种“更地道的”、“更准确的”或“更真实的”模拟，故填形容词 accurate / realistic / exact / precise / correct / true。

57.note: 在状语从句中，主语为单数代词 it（指代地球），后接介词短语 like when...。用来形容外观特征，指球状地球仪展现出的地球，正是它在太空中被观测时所“呈现出的”样子，完美契合专属搭配 looks like（或 appears / seems）。

58.note: 用来修饰复数名词 maps。后文将其与现代地图（modern maps）进行了对比，指代“早期的（early）”、“古老的（ancient）”或者是“过去的（past）”地图，其上往往通过画小城堡来标记地点。

59.note: 动词不定式符号 to 后接动词原形表目的。后接 that 引导的宾语从句，指为了“确保（ensure / make sure）”这些手绘图画清晰可辨，古人会将它们画在巨幅画布上。

60.note: 位于句首且后面有逗号隔开。前文赞美过去的地图好看又易懂，后文突然指出随着细节增多，画面开始变得极其杂乱。前后句存在明显的转折逻辑，可填入转折连词 However 或者是 Yet。位于句首需大写。

61.note: 与后置词 time 完美结合。属于各类地质、历史发展及演变文体中极其核心和高频的段首时间推进句式 Over time，意为“随着时间的推移”或“久而久之”，地图开始走向扁平化与精简。

62.concept: 一般过去时短语动词搭配
62.note: 主语为复数名词 Modern mapmakers（现代地图制作者）。指他们在过去的技术革命中，彻底用符号“替代了”传统的繁琐手绘图画，完美契合经典专属动作搭配 replace A with B，需填入过去时形式 replaced（填入 substituted 需接 for，故 replaced 唯一正确）。

63.concept: 被动语态介词固定搭配
63.note: 前面有动词过去分词形式 represented（被表示/被指代）。在英语中，表示某物是由某种特定手段、媒介所呈现的，固定使用被动语态介词短语 be represented by...（填入 through 表达通过某种符号亦符合语法逻辑）。

64.note: 与前置的介词 For 完美组合，后面有逗号隔开。填入名词 example 或 instance 构成经典固定短语 For example 或 For instance（例如），用以引出黑红相间的双线代指主干道的具体例子。

65.concept: 对比结构分词固定搭配
65.note: 后接介词短语 to maps with drawings。填入过去分词 Compared 构成极其高频的跨时空对比句式 Compared to...（与……相比），用以总结现代符号地图信息量更大且更容易阅读的优势。位于句首需大写。

lines.1: He was not good enough. Not serious enough. Not hardworking enough. Not. Not. Not.
lines.2: Competing in races, compiling achievements, comparing results. Hwa could not understand how or
lines.3: why these things mattered so much to people around him. In school. At home. It was as if they
lines.4: needed invisible yardsticks to measure themselves against others, to know where they stood in
lines.5: order to stand up tall. "First place and nothing less", they say. Such suffocating expectations.
lines.6: And yet here he was, in a line with other windsurfers, **all of them** bobbing nervously on the
lines.7: waves behind an imaginary starting line. They were all fighting for the best position to start and tense
lines.8: as a recruit. It seemed so silly to Hwa, given the whole expanse of the sea. Hwa moved away. How
lines.9: Li-An had talked him into doing this, he did not know. As usual, she had managed to get her way by
lines.10: coaxing, scolding, mocking, daring him. Just as she had always done since they were little.
lines.11: Hwa had never been excited by races. He had not even bothered to wear the digital watch that everyone
lines.12: else seemed to be wearing to time the very second they start. Yet, Hwa's reaction was so natural
lines.13: and quick that at the very moment the starter's horn sounded, he was off. Hwa pulled hard at his
lines.14: sail to race just ahead of the group. As he picked up speed, skimming over the waves, he began to feel
lines.15: the familiar joy and freedom that windsurfing always gave him, despite his earlier doubts. What he
lines.16: loved was simply being out at sea. He could barely stop himself from yelling out in exhilaration.
lines.17: "Go Hwa!" The wind carried over a familiar voice. He looked around and spotted Li-An
lines.18: upwind of him — in a stationary speedboat — with someone at the helm. She waved at Hwa and he
lines.19: nodded his head in acknowledgement, even though he knew she was too far away to see him. Just
lines.20: as he turned away, however, out of the corner of his eye, he saw a twirl of smoke behind the
lines.21: speedboat, on the shore. Knowing that the smoke could tell him the direction the wind was blowing,
lines.22: he decided to study it for a moment out of habit. Just as he was getting a better sense of how to use
lines.23: the wind to his advantage, he saw it
lines.24: Not just the smoke but a bright flare — like an explosion or a burst of flames. He sailed closer,
lines.25: going way off course and saw long tongues of flames licking at the sky from behind a construction
lines.26: site. The fire was definitely spreading. What if nobody was aware of **this**? What if nobody was
lines.27: working there now? It was after all a quiet Sunday afternoon. For a second he hesitated, then
lines.28: decisively swung his sail over and stepped deftly onto the other side of the board until the sail caught
lines.29: the wind from the other side. Hwa directed his surfboard at Li-An's speedboat, avoiding a few of the
lines.30: slower surfers who were lagging behind. "Fire!" Hwa shouted when he got within earshot of Li-An.
lines.31: She stared at him, clearly confused. "Wrong way!" she shouted back. "Fire! Fire!" Hwa yelled again,
lines.32: waving one hand towards land in the direction of the smoke. "Call 995!" She looked at where he was
lines.33: pointing, saw the smoke and understood **his intent**. Hwa waited long enough to see Li-An talking
lines.34: into her mobile phone urgently before turning his attention to the race.
lines.35: The others were far ahead of him now. A gust of fresh wind had sprung up — too good to be
lines.36: wasted — and Hwa swung about to meet it full on. Hwa laughed out loud in exhilaration at the rhythm
lines.37: of the wind and wave that started to surround him.
lines.38: Back on land after the race, the crowd started to surround him. "Good job, third place," he was being
lines.39: told — good enough for the bronze medal. Those words sounded strange, almost like a taunt. So finally
lines.40: he was seen as "good enough"? Whatever happened to the "nots"?
lines.41: "And in third place," the announcement blared from the speaker system, "even with having
lines.42: made the detour to raise the warning about the fire! A tremendous achievement by…” Hwa heard
lines.43: his name being announced, and then the sound of applause and cheering.

paragraphs.1: 他总觉得自己不够好、不够认真、不够用功。不够。不够。不够。比赛、攒成就、比成绩——华不明白身边的人为何如此看重这些。在学校、在家里，仿佛人人都需要一把看不见的标尺，拿来和别人比，好知道自己站在什么位置，才敢抬头挺胸。他们说：“要第一名，否则不算。”这样的期望令人窒息。
paragraphs.6: 然而此刻他却和其他风帆冲浪者排成一行，大家紧张地在假想的起跑线后随波起伏。他们都在同一片水域争抢最佳起步位置，紧张得像新兵。华觉得这很可笑——大海那么开阔。他挪开一些。李安是怎么说服他来的，他也说不清。照例，她又哄又骂又嘲又激，才让他就范，就像打小以来一直那样。
paragraphs.11: 华从不热衷比赛。他甚至懒得戴人人都戴的电子表，好精确到秒起跑。然而发令号一响，他的反应自然而迅速，立刻冲了出去。他用力拉帆，抢在众人前面。加速、掠过浪头时，他再度感到风帆冲浪带来的熟悉快乐与自由，尽管先前还有疑虑。他所爱的，只是身在海上。他几乎忍不住欢呼出声。
paragraphs.17: “加油，华！”风送来熟悉的声音。他环顾四周，看见李安在上风处——停着的快艇上——有人掌舵。她朝华挥手，他点头致意，明知她离得太远看不见。他刚转过身，眼角却瞥见快艇后方、岸上有烟缕升起。他知道烟能告诉他风向，便出于习惯看了一会儿。正当他对如何利用风力更有把握时，他看见了——
paragraphs.24: 不只是烟，还有明亮的火光——像爆炸或火焰迸发。他驶近，大幅偏离航线，看见工地后方的火焰长长舔向天空。火显然在蔓延。要是没人察觉怎么办？要是现在没人施工怎么办？毕竟是安静的周日午后。他犹豫了一秒，随即果断调帆，轻巧换到板另一侧，直到帆再次兜住风。华把冲浪板朝向李安的快艇，避开几个落后的选手。靠近能听见彼此说话时，他大喊：“着火！”李安盯着他，一脸困惑。“方向错了！”她回喊。“火！火！”华又喊，一只手朝岸上烟雾方向挥去。“打995！”她顺着他指的方向看去，看见烟，明白了他的意思。华等到见她急切打电话，才把注意力转回比赛。
paragraphs.35: 别人已遥遥领先。一阵新风突起——太好，不能浪费——华迎风转板，迎头赶上。他放声大笑，沉醉于包围自己的风浪节奏。
paragraphs.38: 比赛结束回到岸上，人群围了上来。“干得好，第三名，”人们说——够拿铜牌了。这些话听起来怪异，几乎像嘲讽。他终于算“够好”了？那些“不够”怎么说就没了？
paragraphs.41: 扩音器高声宣布：“第三名，”即使他绕道去报火情！“了不起的成就，由……”华听见自己的名字被念出，接着是掌声与欢呼。

71.note:
1. 第一段（行 1–5）写他人用 invisible yardsticks 比较；Such suffocating expectations 表 Hwa 对这种做法的感受。
  2. 故摘 suffocating。

72.note:

  2. (b) 上岸后不能再与风浪玩耍 / 暂时无法冲浪等。
